scope: Original B3 endpoint-bound verdicts14/6 retained; corrected locators/observations and source-wide reviewer verdicts18/2 recorded separately; purposive sample.

rows.tested_assertion: 985 selected inscribed objects
rows.B3_observation: 985 is printed in the site table; section 5.1 defines the selected legible/partly legible population.

rows.tested_assertion: 1540 selected inscribed objects
rows.B3_observation: 1540 is printed in the same table; overall selected count is 2906 after 549 exclusions from 3455 photographed objects.

rows.tested_assertion: 28 early pottery-mark drawings not photographed in CISI2
rows.B3_observation: The CISI editors give 28 published drawings and say they could not locate the objects for photography. Dales 1974 itself was not opened in B3.

rows.tested_assertion: 68 reported marked sherds and 10 photographed catalogue entries
rows.B3_observation: The introduction attributes 68 to Halim 1972 and states partial photographic recovery. The plates show Skh1–10. Halim was not opened in B3.

rows.tested_assertion: Rhd267–269 classified as tentative scrapers
rows.B3_observation: Three separate objects and the tentative scraper caption are visible; multiple sides do not add objects.

rows.tested_assertion: Frenez and Tosi report 93 sealings and attribute the total to Rao's finds, pp.67–68,70–71
rows.B3_observation: 93 occurs in the saved article. The review checked its attribution to Rao; it is not a new recount. Rao1985 p.305 reports91 and remains unseen by B3.

rows.locator: saved mirror pp.233,242,308; page numerals follow the preceding text
rows.tested_assertion: 225 recovered seals, 139/194 inscription-positive analysed seals, 60–61 sealings
rows.B3_observation: All figures occur in the saved report text. The inscription table totals 194; the sealing prose contains inconsistent subtraction. Original page rasters were not acquired.

rows.tested_assertion: 26+188+8 broadly marked sherds
rows.B3_observation: The page gives all three groups explicitly. Their sum is 222; the groups include figurative and linear motifs.

rows.tested_assertion: two script-bearing seals plus one sealing
rows.B3_observation: The source describes one steatite seal, one copper seal and a lettered terracotta sealing.

rows.tested_assertion: one Harappan-inscribed clay sealing
rows.B3_observation: The antiquity list describes a clay lump with inscription above a bull impression.

rows.tested_assertion: catalogue endpoint K122
rows.B3_observation: The page labels K122 and its enlarged views. B3 checks the endpoint, not every intervening entry in the batch count of 122.

rows.tested_assertion: catalogue endpoint B37
rows.B3_observation: The page shows B30–37. B3 checks this endpoint and class, not all earlier entries in the batch count of 37.

rows.locator: graffiti p.120 / PDF125; seals pp.114,117 / PDF119,122; plates pp.118–119
rows.tested_assertion: 157 graffiti instances, comprising 134+22+1
rows.B3_observation: The report gives 134 sherd instances, 22 spindle-whorl instances and one ring instance. It separately describes two inscribed seals.

rows.tested_assertion: two marked tablets and nineteen marked sherds
rows.B3_observation: P.139 lists two tablets and nineteen marked sherds. Fig.39 draws A-1 in three views; A-2 is described in the text and listed by the review in Pl.XLIII B.

rows.tested_assertion: Rhr1–2 seal impressions
rows.B3_observation: Both labels and images are visible. They are separate from the Rojdi and Rupar material on the same page.

rows.locator: catalogue p.113 / PDF151; discussion pp.81–82 / PDF119–120
rows.tested_assertion: 13 N 506, IM78230, one inscribed seal
rows.B3_observation: Catalogue p.113 supplies registrations13 N506/IM78230, dimensions2×2×1cm and Floor3. The deliberate-fill heading below belongs to other objects; pp.81–82 discuss secondary context.

rows.tested_assertion: Sh1–84 mixed catalogue; two seals reported
rows.B3_observation: The contents give 84 mixed entries; the preface describes two seals and plentiful graffiti. This does not verify two separate script-bearing seals.

rows.tested_assertion: TY1–112 mixed catalogue and an Indus seal impression TY106
rows.B3_observation: Both the sequence and the specific seal-impression attribution appear in the source. The 112-entry total includes other scripts and glyptics.

rows.tested_assertion: one seal and two impressed fragments, possibly one vessel
rows.B3_observation: The seal and first fragment are described separately. The later rim impression is stated to be possibly from the same jar.

rows.locator: p.258 / PDF130, figs.114–115; narrative continues p.259
rows.tested_assertion: one elephant seal with signs, separate from a cuneiform cylinder
rows.B3_observation: The spread illustrates a seal and its impression in figure114 and a different cylinder in figure115. The narrative places the elephant seal in room19, area9.
